Yes—very likely.

The Moon is **16.2° above the horizon**, toward **azimuth 231°** (southwest), and it’s **25% illuminated**. At that altitude and separation from the Sun (**60°**), it should be well clear of the worst glare. In bright Mumbai daylight it may be faint, but a clear sky and normal eyesight should be enough.

Look **southwest**, about **16° above the horizon**—roughly one and a half fist-widths at arm’s length above the horizon. It will be a thin-ish **waning crescent**, with the illuminated side facing generally toward the Sun (roughly southeast). Avoid looking anywhere near the Sun itself, and use a building or other obstruction to block direct sunlight. Binoculars could help you acquire it, but don’t use them unless you are certain the Sun cannot enter the view.
